clue.text: Doctors giving up rounds kept within peaceful boundary

indicators.note: something kept within another sits inside it, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: peaceful means quiet

indicators.note: a piece that gives something up loses those letters

parts.note: to doctor accounts is to cook them, so doctors means cooks
rounds are round shapes, the letter O twice

explanation.surface: Medics stop doing their ward rounds and stay inside a tranquil perimeter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctors' looks like medics but is a verb, as in doctoring the books; 'giving up' removes both Os, and 'kept within' places the remainder inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A quickset is a hedge grown from cuttings, which serves as a living boundary round a field or garden.

clue.text: Intrude, surprising virgin

indicators.note: a surprising arrangement is an unexpected one, signalling rearranged letters

explanation.surface: An unexpected visitor intrudes on someone innocent.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgin as an adjective means untouched or never used, like an untried idea.

clue.text: Moths will emerge

definitions.meaning: moths are drawn to a lamp

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to become known, and moths literally fly towards any lamp.

clue.text: One with bowl quickly collects coin

indicators.note: a word that collects another takes it inside

parts.note: soon means quickly, before long
P is a penny, the smallest British coin

explanation.surface: A bowler hurries to pick up a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoon is an implement made of a bowl on a handle.

clue.text: Short book on rodents and birds

parts.note: Tit. is the short form of Titus, a book of the Bible
mice are rodents

explanation.surface: A slim volume about small rodents and birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Titmice are small songbirds, the tit family, so they are examples of birds.

clue.text: Remove one's name from plan?

definitions.meaning: read as ..., to take back one's signature
a plan or scheme for something

explanation.definitionFit: A design is a plan or drawing made before building something; split in two, de-sign suggests unsigning.

clue.text: Neglected dated fuel supply

indicators.note: read as an adverb, supple-ly, the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned fuel stocks were overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a noun, but read as 'supplely' (in a supple way) it means the letters are bent.
explanation.definitionFit: To default is to fail to do what was due, so defaulted means neglected a duty.

clue.text: Runner introducing some kinky innovations

indicators.note: introducing letters are those at the start of each word

explanation.surface: An athlete brings in some odd new ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski is a runner, the long narrow piece under a sledge or a skier's boot.

clue.text: Travel with wife and split the cost

parts.note: to travel is to go
Dutch is Cockney slang for wife, from duchess

explanation.surface: A couple go away together and share expenses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my old Dutch' is Cockney (London) slang for a wife.
explanation.definitionFit: To go Dutch is the idiom for each person paying their own share.

clue.text: Mental relaxation first seen in the year dot

definitions.meaning: read literally, a break taken away from one's mind

definitions.text: first seen in the year dot
definitions.meaning: dating from so long ago that nobody remembers

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means for longer than anyone can remember, so something from that time dates from the year dot.

clue.text: Silent, prepared to pay attention

indicators.note: the letters are made ready in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone stays quiet, ready to take notice.
explanation.definitionFit: To listen is to pay attention to sounds or speech, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Entertaining sister, I had had a meal in swamp

indicators.note: a host entertaining a guest holds them, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd
a nun is a religious sister
had a meal means ate

explanation.surface: Someone apologises for a big lunch while hosting a sister in a marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan prints 'had' twice, once for the contraction and once for the meal; the held text drops one.
explanation.definitionFit: To swamp is to flood or overwhelm, which is exactly what inundate means.

clue.text: Setting down and going to sleep

definitions.meaning: letting a passenger out of a car

explanation.definitionFit: A taxi is dropping off a fare when it sets them down; a drowsy person is dropping off when falling asleep.

clue.text: A handout's very little money for a juvenile

parts.note: the dole is a state handout; with 's it gives DOLES
a cent is a coin of tiny value

explanation.surface: A benefit payment is worth next to nothing to a young person.
explanation.definitionFit: A juvenile is a young person, and an adolescent is a teenager, so the nouns match.

clue.text: Lush —- man following copper hither and thither in the street

indicators.note: one piece goes in another

parts.note: St is short for street

indicators.note: copper is written going one way and then the other

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
Len is a man's name

explanation.surface: A drunk man trails a policeman back and forth along the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hither and thither' writes the copper symbol both ways round (UC, then CU), and 'following' sets the man after it, all within the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Lush vegetation is juicy and full, as succulent plants are, so the adjectives match.

clue.text: Man, the one in command on the front line

parts.note: OC is the military abbreviation for Officer Commanding
a man is he

explanation.surface: A soldier and his commanding officer stand at the front of battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The oche is the line a darts player stands behind to throw, a sense far from the battlefield the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: In darts the oche is the mark players toe when throwing, the line at the front of play.

clue.text: Pine bought in advance

definitions.meaning: on the stock market, holding shares bought in expectation of a rise

explanation.definitionFit: To long is to yearn or pine; in finance, going long means buying ahead of an expected rise.

clue.text: Former employee finally comes in punctually

indicators.note: one letter comes into the middle of a longer piece

parts.note: punctually means on time

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: An ex-worker at last turns up when due.
explanation.definitionFit: Onetime is an adjective meaning former or erstwhile, as in a onetime champion.

clue.text: Piece of cake, little one, spread out

parts.note: a little one is a child
to splay is to spread out

explanation.surface: A slice of cake and a small child sprawled on the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for a task that is very easy to do.

clue.text: Some like bananas in very special arrangement

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people are fond of bananas arranged just so.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikebana is the Japanese art of flower arranging, a highly refined kind of arrangement.

clue.text: Investigators employed in federal bureau come up with self-discipline

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means reading from the bottom
employed in a body means working inside it

parts.note: the CIA is a US federal intelligence agency
tecs is slang for detectives

explanation.surface: Detectives working for the FBI turn out to be very disciplined.
explanation.walkthrough: TECS goes into CIA for CITECSA; 'come up' reverses it in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascetic describes someone who lives austerely and denies themselves pleasures, with self-discipline.

clue.text: Puzzle engrossing king and naughty queen

indicators.note: to engross is to take in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to get someone is to puzzle them, as in 'you've got me there'
R is short for rex, Latin for king
naughty means rude

explanation.surface: A riddle about a king and a wayward queen.
explanation.walkthrough: GET 'engrossing' R gives GERT; add RUDE. Gertrude is the queen in Hamlet who marries her husband's killer, so 'naughty' fits her.
explanation.definitionFit: Gertrude is the Queen of Denmark in Shakespeare's Hamlet, an example of a queen.

clue.text: Two cards stick around in the outskirts of Tonbridge

indicators.note: one piece goes in another
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters
turned around means read the other way

parts.note: a cane is a stick

explanation.surface: Someone plays cards near the edge of Tonbridge, a town in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the stick to ENAC; Tonbridge is a town in Kent whose first and last letters enclose it.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge and whist a tenace is a holding of two high cards, such as ace and queen, missing the one between.

clue.text: Agreement to take year off is pleasant surprise

indicators.note: taking a piece away from a word removes it
off as in 'take a day off', meaning the named letter is cut away from the agreement word

parts.note: a treaty is an agreement

explanation.surface: A deal giving a year off work is a nice surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A treat is something unexpected that gives pleasure, a nice surprise.

clue.text: Cat and owl were sharing difficult circumstances

definitions.meaning: in Edward Lear's poem the owl and the pussycat go to sea in a pea-green boat together
facing the same trouble as others

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means sharing a predicament; Lear's owl and pussycat literally shared one vessel.

clue.text: Yank's stomach upset

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, read bottom up

parts.note: the gut is the stomach

explanation.surface: An American has a bad tummy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank's' looks like an American, but it is the verb, with 's for is.
explanation.definitionFit: To yank is to pull sharply, which is what a tug is.

clue.text: Told to hang on, being a burden

indicators.note: told means spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to hang on is to wait

explanation.surface: Someone asked to wait feels they are a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: A weight is a heavy load or responsibility, a synonym for burden.

clue.text: Trick has worked if I react

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A ruse succeeds if I respond the way it wants.
explanation.definitionFit: Artifice is cunning or a crafty device meant to deceive, a trick.
